exposure: maternal secretor status (secreting a1-2 fucosylated HMOs in breast milk)
cohort: The study included cesarean and vaginally born infants who were exclusively breastfed by mothers secreting a1-2 fucosylated oligosaccharides in breast milk.
finding: Cesarean and vaginally born infants fed with breast milk containing a1-2 fucosylated HMOs present similar amounts of Bifidobacterium in the feces, but differences are observed in other members of the microbiota.
mod_finding: Cesarean born infants, despite being fed by secretor mothers, showed lower prevalence of B. longum and lower relative abundance of Bacteroides, while Akkermansia and Kluyvera were higher, compared to vaginally born infants.
